title: $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ is thick and essentially small
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning quasi-compact and locally Noetherian, and use the fixed-universe small-site convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. Let $\Lambda$ be an admissible commutative condensed coefficient ring: a finite discrete commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$, or $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Qlb$, with the coefficient objects of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Let $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ and write $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)=D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ for the ordinary unbounded derived category of its module objects. Write $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ for the full subcategory of bounded complexes with constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. Then $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ is a thick triangulated subcategory of $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ [pur9-def-thick], and it is essentially small, meaning that its objects have a set of representatives up to isomorphism in that fixed universe.

proof.text: Work in the fixed universe and small-site skeleton convention. Put $\mathcal M=\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ and $\mathcal T=D(\mathcal M)$. The sheaf-tensor structure theorem supplies abelian sheafification and its strong symmetric monoidal structure on this small site, so the hypotheses of the internal/sectionwise equivalence hold. That equivalence identifies $\mathcal M$ with sheaves of modules over the corresponding ring sheaf, preserving underlying abelian sheaves and restrictions. The small ringed-site theorem makes this category Grothendieck abelian. For two module sheaves, their morphisms are a subset of the product, over the small site, of the sets of sectionwise module homomorphisms, hence form a small set. The Grothendieck category therefore has K-injective resolutions, and the locally-small-derived-category theorem gives small ambient Hom sets, in the same universe as the site and coefficient modules. In particular all Hom sets used in the counting argument below are small; this does not assume that the collection of all objects of $\mathcal M$ is small.

source.place: Essentially small paragraph: ambient Hom sets; Stacks 09PA, remark-existence-derived

proof.text: First treat a finite discrete admissible ring $A$. The finite-discrete condensed/constant-ring isomorphism and its scheme pullback identify the pulled-back coefficient ring with the sheafified constant ring. The internal-module equivalence in abelian groups supplies the scalar encoding $G$; use the common encoding $E_T$ on each scheme $T$. The restriction comparison identifies $j^*(E_X^{-1}M)$ with the encoded restriction of $M$ for every stratum immersion $j$. Thus an internal constructible module gives an intrinsically constructible ordinary $A$-module sheaf. Conversely, a local constant finite $A$-module $P$ is finitely presented (a surjection from a finite free module has finite, hence finitely generated, kernel), and its internal image is the scalar local model $A_T\otimes_A P$: write $P$ as a cokernel of a matrix $A^m\to A^n$; the encoding sends the constant regular module to the regular internal module and preserves finite sums and cokernels, so the encoded presentation is the same scalar matrix on $A_T^m\to A_T^n$. Applying this on the same finite stratification proves the converse. Consequently $E_X$ identifies the two constructible hearts. As an equivalence of abelian categories it preserves kernels and cokernels by their universal properties; applying it termwise therefore gives a derived equivalence preserving cohomology and cone triangles. This coefficient identification is used only for finite discrete $A$.

source.place: Thick and Essentially small paragraphs: finite discrete local models and coefficient identification

proof.text: For finite $A$, the equivalence between intrinsically constructible pro-étale and étale sheaves reduces smallness of the heart to the étale case. Choose a small skeleton of the étale site. A finite ring is Noetherian because every ideal is a finite set and its elements generate it. The locally-Noetherian quasi-separatedness theorem applies to $X$; together with its assumed quasi-compactness this makes $X$ qcqs. Therefore the affine-free presentation theorem applies: every constructible étale $A$-module is a cokernel of a map between two finite sums of free sheaves $A[h_U]$, with $U$ affine étale. Finite lists of objects of the chosen site form a set, and for each pair of lists the maps between the corresponding free sheaves form a set. Choose one cokernel for each such map. Their set of isomorphism classes contains every constructible étale sheaf, so the finite-coefficient constructible heart is essentially small. This counts presentations, not all arbitrary sheaves on the site.

source.place: Essentially small paragraph: finite presentations and sheaves on a fixed small site; Stacks 095N and 09AK

proof.text: For $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, the coefficient-heart closure theorem gives kernels, cokernels and extensions in the ambient module category, and the coefficient-heart smallness theorem supplies a set of representatives. For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, apply the integral scalar-constant heart-closure lemma: its coefficient object is the same $p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$, and its local models are exactly the finitely presented scalar-module models in the definition used here. It gives ambient kernels, cokernels and extensions under the present Noetherian hypothesis, without imposing a ground field or finite-type hypothesis on $X$. Integral-heart smallness is proved in steps 5–7. The cases $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $\mathbf Z_\ell$ are respectively $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and its valuation ring. Zero is constructible by its rank-zero local model.

source.place: Thick and Essentially small paragraphs: rational hearts and integral scalar-constant heart closure; Bhatt–Scholze Definition 6.8.10, Proposition 6.8.11(1)

proof.text: Fix integral coefficients and one stratum $T$. Its pro-étale site has a small skeleton in the fixed universe. For the weakly étale objects of a covering, the localization theorem identifies their pro-étale sites with the corresponding slice sites; cartesian coefficients identify the restrictions of the coefficient sheaves. Thus the local model identifications can be read as ordinary restrictions of module sheaves on those slices. Finitely presented scalar $\mathcal O_E$-modules have a set of representatives: take cokernels of all finite matrices over the set $\mathcal O_E$. The finite constant local model definition says that any local-model sheaf on $T$ is given on a covering family by the corresponding sheaves $R_U\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}P$. Cover families can be chosen from a set by removing repeated arrows in the small site, and assignments of these scalar presentations form a set. Between two fixed model sheaves on an overlap, morphisms form a set: they are natural linear families in the product of sectionwise function sets over the small slice site. Thus overlap isomorphisms satisfying the cocycle condition form a set. These data determine a realization up to isomorphism: local identifications of two realizations agree on overlaps, so the equalizer sheaf axiom glues a unique morphism on sections; glue the inverses too. The glued maps are natural and linear because these properties hold locally and the sheaf axiom detects equality. Retain only data having a realization and choose one realization for each. This gives a set of local-model sheaves on every fixed stratum, without asserting effectivity for arbitrary descent data.

source.place: Essentially small paragraph: integral local presentations, covers and overlap data

proof.text: For a finite stratification $(a_s:T_s\to X)_s$ and a tuple of local-model sheaves $F_s$ from step 5, form the finite product $P=\prod_s a_{s*}F_s$. The module pushforward/pullback adjunction and cartesian coefficient statement give $a_s^*\dashv a_{s*}$, with $a_s^*$ exact and its underlying abelian-sheaf functor equal to $a_s^{-1}$ up to the stated canonical natural isomorphism. For a constructible module $F$ with chosen $\varphi_s:a_s^*F\simeq F_s$, define $u:F\to P$ by $u_s=a_{s*}(\varphi_s)\circ\eta_{s,F}$. Let $N=\ker u$. Exactness identifies $a_s^*N$ with $\ker(a_s^*u)$. The component $a_s^*u_s$ has left inverse $\varepsilon_{s,a_s^*F}\circ a_s^*a_{s*}(\varphi_s^{-1})$: its composite with $a_s^*u_s$ is the identity by the adjunction triangle identity. Thus this component is monic and $a_s^*N=0$. On underlying abelian sheaves this says $a_s^{-1}U(N)=0$ for every $s$. Apply the Noetherian finite-stratum zero-detection theorem with identity covers on the strata to get $U(N)=0$, hence $N=0$. Therefore every such $F$ embeds in $P$. Only untwisted $\mathcal O_E$ coefficients are used, so the cartesian theorem requires no invertibility hypothesis on $X$.

source.place: Essentially small paragraph: global sheaves determined by stratum data, made explicit by an adjunction-unit embedding; Stacks 09AH and 09AB via the cited detection theorem

proof.text: The finite stratifications of the fixed bounded scheme $X$ form a set: choose finite lists of locally closed subsets and bounded scheme structures and immersion maps with those images. For each stratification, step 5 supplies a set of tuples $(F_s)_s$, hence a set of sheaves $P$ in step 6. For fixed $P$, its subobjects form a set directly. Kernels of module-sheaf maps are computed sectionwise, so a monomorphism is sectionwise injective and may be identified with its image subsheaf. Such an image specifies a subset of $P(V)$ for every object $V$ of the small site, subject to restriction, module and sheaf axioms. All these choices lie in the set $\prod_V\mathcal P(P(V))$. Taking their union over the set of $P$ gives a set of representatives for all integral constructible sheaves by step 6. This proves integral-heart essential smallness under the original Noetherian hypothesis. For empty $X$, the empty stratification gives the zero module sheaf and the argument includes it.

source.place: Essentially small paragraph: integral global gluing counted as subobjects of a set of fixed sheaves

proof.text: For finite $A$, apply the inverse derived equivalence of step 2 to a triangle of internal modules. It remains distinguished and its cohomology is the ordinary encoding of the internal cohomology. The bounded-constructible pro-étale theorem puts the third vertex in the ordinary bounded-constructible subcategory whenever the other two are there. Applying the derived equivalence back, and using its identification of constructible hearts from step 2, proves the corresponding closure for internal modules; the zero object and shifts are preserved as well. Thus $\Dbc(X,A)$ is triangulated. For the other coefficients, apply the weak-Serre cohomology theorem to the zero-containing heart in step 4: closure under kernels, cokernels and extensions is precisely its hypothesis. This gives that $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ is triangulated. Concretely, shifts reindex cohomology, and for a triangle $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$ the long exact cohomology sequence gives a short exact sequence with middle term $H^n(L)$, left term $\operatorname{coker}(H^{n-1}(M)\to H^n(K))$ and right term $\ker(H^n(M)\to H^{n+1}(K))$. Thus constructibility and a finite cohomological range are preserved. In the finite case we will also need kernel closure in the heart: for $F,G$ in that heart, the cone of $F[0]\to G[0]$ is bounded constructible, and its cohomology in degrees $-1,0$ is respectively the kernel and cokernel of $F\to G$. This follows from the same long exact sequence.

source.place: Thick paragraph: bounded constructibility under shifts and triangles

proof.text: Let $L$ be an ambient retract of $K\in\Dbc$: choose $i:L\to K$ and $r:K\to L$ with $ri=1_L$. Functoriality gives $H^n(r)H^n(i)=1$, so $H^n(L)$ is zero whenever $H^n(K)$ is zero. On $H^n(K)$ put $e=H^n(i)H^n(r)$. The split monomorphism $H^n(i)$ identifies $H^n(L)$ with $\ker(1-e)$: $(1-e)H^n(i)=0$, and any $x$ with $(1-e)x=0$ satisfies $x=H^n(i)H^n(r)x$. The kernel closure of the appropriate heart from steps 4 and 8 makes this sheaf constructible. Hence $\Dbc$ is closed under all ambient retracts. Together with step 8 and the definition of thick, it is a thick subcategory.

source.place: Thick paragraph: direct summands of constructible cohomology

proof.text: The well-definedness assertions of the Tor-amplitude node give closure of finite Tor amplitude under shifts, triangles and retracts for these same internal module categories. The interval bookkeeping is as follows. A shift $K[n]$ changes $[a,b]$ to $[a-n,b-n]$. If the first and third terms of a triangle have finite amplitude, enlarge their intervals to a common interval $[a,b]$; the middle term then has amplitude in $[a,b]$. In particular, if $K\to L\to C\to K[1]$ is a cone triangle with $K$ of amplitude $[a_K,b_K]$ and $L$ of amplitude $[a_L,b_L]$, rotate and use the bounds for $L$ and $K[1]$: $C$ has amplitude in $[\min(a_L,a_K-1),\max(b_L,b_K-1)]$. A retract has the same amplitude bound as the object of which it is a retract. Therefore $\Dctf=\Dbc\cap\{\text{finite Tor amplitude}\}$ is an intersection of thick subcategories, and is thick: each closure operation preserves both defining predicates. In particular this argument does not assert that standard truncation preserves finite Tor amplitude.

source.place: Thick paragraph: finite Tor amplitude; corrected cone interval

proof.text: Choose a set $S$ of representatives for the constructible heart, using steps 3, 4 and 7. For a complex $K$ with constructible cohomology supported in $[a,b]$, put $T_q=\tau_{\leq q}K$. The explicit truncation formula shows that $H^r(T_q)=H^r(K)$ for $r\leq q$ and zero for $r>q$: below $q$ the differential is unchanged and at $q$ the quotient is $\ker(d^q)/\operatorname{im}(d^{q-1})$. Thus $T_{a-1}\simeq0$ and $T_b\simeq K$ by quasi-isomorphisms, and the truncation-step triangle is $T_{q-1}\to T_q\to H^q(K)[-q]\xrightarrow{\delta_q}T_{q-1}[1]$. These are truncations in the ambient $D(\mathcal M)$; no Tor condition is imposed on them.

source.place: Essentially small paragraph: ambient truncation triangles

proof.text: Fix integers $a\leq b$ and construct a set of representatives for bounded constructible objects with cohomology in $[a,q]$, by induction on $q=a-1,\ldots,b$. Start at $q=a-1$ with the single zero object. Given a set $R_{q-1}$ covering all isomorphism classes at the previous stage, consider every pair $B\in R_{q-1}$, $C\in S$ and every morphism $f:C[-q-1]\to B$. These morphisms range over a set by step 1. Choose one cone for each $f$ and retain those cones with constructible cohomology in $[a,q]$; this is still a set. Every $K$ in this interval occurs up to isomorphism: step 11 and inverse rotation express it as a cone of $-\delta_q[-1]:H^q(K)[-q-1]\to T_{q-1}$. Choose isomorphisms $\beta:T_{q-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ and $\gamma:H^q(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}C$. The counted arrow is explicitly $f=\beta\circ(-\delta_q[-1])\circ\gamma[-q-1]^{-1}$. Replacing the first two vertices by these isomorphic representatives gives a distinguished triangle starting with $f$ and having third vertex isomorphic to $K$. Cones of a fixed arrow are isomorphic: TR3 extends the identities on the first two vertices to a triangle morphism, and the two-isomorphisms theorem makes its third component invertible. Thus the chosen cone covers $K$. This proves the induction, including $q=a$, when the previous term is zero; it does not require a functorial cone.

source.place: Essentially small paragraph: induction on the cohomological interval; Stacks 014B and 014A

proof.text: Take the union of the representative sets in step 12 over the set of pairs $(a,b)\in\mathbf Z^2$ with $a\leq b$. It covers every bounded constructible object, so $\Dbc$ is essentially small. Finite Tor amplitude is invariant under isomorphism. Retain exactly those representatives with finite Tor amplitude; any $K\in\Dctf$ is isomorphic to a retained representative. The full subcategory $\Dctf$ is therefore essentially small. If $X$ is empty or the coefficient ring is zero, all these categories have only the zero object up to isomorphism and the same construction applies.

source.place: Essentially small paragraph: all bounded ranges and the full finite-Tor subcategory

split_report.summary: Repaired the landing refusal against the current DAG. The changed integral-heart lemma now assumes separated finite type over a positive-characteristic field; those hypotheses are not present here, so its citation was removed rather than applied outside its domain. One smaller statement-only lemma records Bhatt–Scholze integral scalar-constant constructible heart closure on any Noetherian scheme. Steps 5–7 prove integral heart smallness using explicit local data, a stratum-adjunction embedding, and a sectionwise subobject count. The retained finite/rational proofs, thick intersection and ambient Postnikov induction give thirteen steps. No hypothesis or conclusion of the item changed in this repair. No complete-category identification or scalar-nonconstant presentation comparison is assumed.
split_report.blueprint: Thick paragraph: steps 2, 4, 8–10. Essentially small paragraph: steps 1, 3–7, 11–13. The integral heart argument expands the source finite presentations/local sheaves/gluing sentence. Ambient truncations occur in step 11.

The repair is correct. The integral-heart node det-lem-int-integral-heart-triangulated is no longer cited: it now assumes X separated of finite type over a field of characteristic p≠ℓ, which a Noetherian X need not satisfy (Spec Z). The item's statement is unchanged from the earlier reviewed split: X Noetherian, the six admissible Λ exactly as in sk-def-localizing-closure, ambient D(Mod_{Λ_X}). It is no weaker than the blueprint, whose proof itself says 'the Noetherian scheme X'. The shifted cone interval [min(a_L,a_K-1),max(b_L,b_K-1)] is correct; the zero map A[0]→A[0] shows the blueprint's unshifted union is wrong. Source check: the new node lem-sfb-integral-constant-model-heart-closure matches Bhatt–Scholze Def 6.8.10 and Prop 6.8.11(1) (printed pp. 60–61; scalar-constant finitely presented O_E models, topologically Noetherian X) hypothesis by hypothesis. It holds on the small cases I tried (empty X, P=0, a geometric point, multiplication by ϖ, torsion extensions). It is not a duplicate: the int-heart nodes need finite type over a field, and lem-weil-pbc-integral-constructible-serre/-kernels/condensed-constructible-serre concern the larger class with non-constant matrix entries. It does not restate the item: it is heart-level closure, the input the blueprint's Thick paragraph names. Steps checked: in step 6 the left inverse ε∘a*a_*(φ⁻¹) composed with a*(u_s) is the identity by the triangle identity, and stratum detection with identity covers then gives ker u=0. Step 3 applies the presentation theorem in the right direction (étale-constructible implies def-constructible-constructible). In step 12, inverse rotation plus TR3 and the two-of-three isomorphism lemma covers every K. Steps 5, 7, 9 and 13 are elementary relative to their citations. Dependencies: no cycle; no missing or merged ids; proof_deps equals the union of uses.
